## [1.11.0] - 2026-08-18

### Added

  for nullable values.

  messaging accounts, birthday and job title. `PersonAddress` is an alias of

  the `nova` user-access app value.

### Changed

- Refresh the official v1 and v2 OpenAPI specifications, re-derive the v1
  legacy surface and regenerate the internal clients.

## [1.10.1] - 2026-08-14

### Changed

- Bump the preferred Go toolchain, CI, security scanning and OpenAPI drift
  checks from Go 1.26.5 to Go 1.26.6. Go 1.25 remains supported.
- Bump `github/codeql-action` from v4.37.5 to v4.37.6, keeping the `init`
  and `analyze` steps on the same pinned revision.

### Security

- Credentials from `Config.Auth` are now attached only to requests whose origin
  matches `Config.BaseURL`. Previously the transport middleware re-applied them
  on every redirect hop, so a cross-origin redirect delivered `x-api-token` and
  OAuth bearer tokens to the redirect target. An unparseable `BaseURL` now fails

  credentials still apply to every first-party request, but a redirect leaving
  the initial request's origin suppresses them on that hop.

  `WithHeader("x-api-token", …)`) are stripped when a redirect leaves the pinned
  origin. `NewHTTPClient` installs a `CheckRedirect` for this; a `CheckRedirect`
  already present on a supplied `HTTPClient` is still called, and the standard
  10-redirect limit is preserved. Credential headers the preserved callback
  re-adds to an off-origin hop are removed again after it returns.
- The v1 OAuth client is built without the `Auth` provider, so an API token is
  no longer sent to the OAuth host.
- Non-2xx response bodies are truncated at 1 MiB. They previously bypassed the
  response size cap entirely and were buffered in full into `APIError.Body`.
- A server-supplied `Retry-After` is capped and no longer overflows when
  converted to a duration.

Done. Both parts of the report are addressed. Changes are left uncommitted for your review (HEAD is detached and you didn't ask for commits).

## Root cause

`http.NewRequestWithContext` only populates `Request.GetBody` for `*bytes.Buffer`, `*bytes.Reader`, and `*strings.Reader`. `Files.Add` passed the caller's `io.Reader` (their `*os.File`) straight through `RawClient.Do`, so `GetBody` was nil — and the retry transport (correctly, per its own contract) refuses to resend a non-replayable body, so 429 failed instantly. Every other call retries fine because JSON bodies and `strings.Reader` form bodies are replayable natively.

## PR notes

**Summary**
- `fix(retry)`: `RawClient.Do` now buffers request bodies that `net/http` can't replay natively (e.g. `*os.File`), so `Files.Add`/`Files.Update` uploads retry on 429/502/503/504 like every other call. `WithNoRetry()` per request keeps the old streaming behavior for very large bodies.
- `feat(v1)`: new `Files.Upload(ctx, fileName, reader, ...)` builds the multipart body for you (via the existing `internal/multipartbody` helper), mirroring `CallLogs.AddRecording`. `Files.Add` stays for full control (extra form fields, custom content types).
- Docs: CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entries + README retry/upload notes.

**Testing performed** (all tests written failing-first)
- `raw_test.go`: reader body retries on 429 with the full payload resent; GetBody set for opaque readers; `WithNoRetry` preserves streaming (no buffering, no retry); body read errors surface before any request is sent.
- `v1/files_test.go`: `Files.Add` with a real `os.Open` file retries on 429 and resends the identical file body (the exact reported scenario); `Upload` multipart encoding (field `file`, filename, payload, custom headers), validation errors, source-read error, and 429 retry.
- `go test ./...` (also `-race` on touched packages), `go vet ./...`, `gofmt` — all clean.

**Breaking changes / migration**
- None. One intentional behavior change: arbitrary `io.Reader` bodies are now buffered in memory (unless the call uses `WithNoRetry()`), which also means `Content-Length` is now set instead of chunked encoding, and the transport no longer closes a caller-owned `*os.File`.
